title: The Drowned Thirteenth Floor
audioNote: Every available clip contains audio. Revised clips use Flow-generated audio or local synthetic English dialogue with ambience. Optional English captions accompany locally voiced clips. Final listening and lip-sync review remains required.

scenes.title: One button too many
text: You are Alex Morgan. It is 12:43 a.m. Your building has twelve floors.
A new button glows beneath the others: B13. You press it. The lift begins to descend.

scenes.title: The hotel below
text: The doors open onto a waterlogged hotel corridor. Salt hangs in the air.
At the far end, an attendant stands with his back to you. He does not turn, even when he speaks.

dialogue.speaker: Attendant
dialogue.line: Welcome back. We have been expecting the surface guest.

scenes.title: Water should fall
text: Droplets pull away from the wet carpet and climb the wall. Nothing on this floor falls the way it should.
Beside you, the emergency telephone starts to ring.
scenes.clue: The water moves upward. This floor does not obey the world above.

scenes.title: Close the doors
text: You press CLOSE DOOR. The brass doors slide shut. For a moment, the lift is silent.

scenes.title: Farther away
scenes.productionNote: New Flow-generated picture and audio. Visual continuity checked; final listening and dialogue review remains required.
text: The doors open again. The corridor stretches much farther into the darkness, but the attendant's voice sounds closer.
The emergency telephone keeps ringing.

dialogue.speaker: Attendant
dialogue.line: Your room has been waiting for a very long time.

scenes.title: Your own voice
text: You lift the receiver. The voice on the other end is yours — older, exhausted, whispering.
The line stays open. You look down: an open guest register lies on the wet carpet beside the lift.

dialogue.speaker: Your voice
dialogue.line: Alex. Don't say your name. Silence this line before you erase it from the book.

scenes.clue: The hotel keeps names it hears. Silence the emergency line before erasing your entry.

scenes.title: You have stayed here before
scenes.productionNote: Revised picture edit with English synthetic dialogue where scripted and added ambience. Final listening review remains required.
text: Only one entry is dry: ALEX MORGAN. Check-in: 17 September 1726. Check-out: —.
A printed rule sits beneath your entry: A name spoken is a name kept.
An antique key rests on the facing page. You can accept the room, try the lift, or remove the reservation.

dialogue.speaker: Attendant
dialogue.line: Would you like to confirm your reservation, Mr Morgan?

scenes.clue: The register lists Alex Morgan as a guest since 1726. Leaving the floor may not end the reservation.

choices.label: Accept the key and step out
Leave the book. Return to ground floor
Erase your name from the register

scenes.title: Check-In
text: You accept the key. The lights go out for a heartbeat.
Light returns. White gloves cover your hands; gold-trimmed uniform cuffs replace your own sleeves.
You know what to say. You must not turn around.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.line: We have been expecting the surface guest.

scenes.productionNote: Flow picture recut to remove unintended fire and reopening; synthetic English dialogue. Automated speech check supplements, but does not replace, final listening review.

scenes.title: Surface
scenes.productionNote: Revised picture edit with English synthetic dialogue where scripted and added ambience. Final listening review remains required.
text: The lift returns to the ground floor. Beyond the glass, your city lies beneath an endless ocean.
Your name is still in the register. The hotel has not let you go. It has brought the world down to meet you.

dialogue.speaker: Your voice
dialogue.line: You left the hotel. Your name didn't.

scenes.title: An empty line
scenes.productionNote: Revised picture edit with English synthetic dialogue where scripted and added ambience. Final listening review remains required.
text: With the emergency line silent, you erase ALEX MORGAN. The date and the rule fade with it.
The page is blank. The reservation is gone. Somewhere inside the lift, the motor starts again.

scenes.title: Nameless
scenes.productionNote: New Flow-generated picture and audio. Visual continuity checked; final listening and dialogue review remains required.
text: The lobby is dry. Ordinary daylight falls across the marble. You think you have escaped.
The doorman has greeted you every morning for ten years. Now he raises his hand and refuses to let you pass.
The hotel has forgotten you. So has everyone else.

dialogue.speaker: Doorman
dialogue.line: I am sorry. Nobody by that name lives here.
